classification.classification_note: The witnessed bug is a fuzzer-side uninitialized read: Stage 01's MSan report traces poison to stack `std::string original` in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, then names the subsequent `std::string(original.c_str())` copy and the later `RegexMatcher::Match` preprocessing as the project-side propagation path into the sink.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42501995 (flatbuffers): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target scalar_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42501995
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` while the staged 3-byte witness `02 14 10` exercised FlatBuffers' `scalar_fuzzer`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` treats byte 0 as `flags`, bypasses the first two control bytes, and therefore wraps the single remaining payload byte `0x10` in stack `std::string original`. The next line constructs `input` from `original.c_str()`, and the saved MSan store stack identifies that statement as the first point where uninitialized bytes were stored to memory on the crashing path; the saved origin ties those bytes back to the stack allocation of `original`. `ScalarReferenceResult::Check` then uses `flags & 0x0f == 0x2` to select the `int8` / `IntegerRegex` matcher, `RegexMatcher::Match` materializes `test = StripString(input, "\t\r\n ", &r.pos)`, and `r.len = test.size()` is the first observed use, with libc++ `std::__1::basic_string::size()` as frame 0 and `RegexMatcher::Match:83` as the first project frame. The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` are unrelated to this path, so the chain below is grounded by the staged vulnerable source and the saved MSan origin/store stacks rather than by a matching fix hunk.

source.description: First project statement on the witnessed path that consumes the fuzz input by materializing the dispatch byte `flags` from `data[0]` and retargeting `data,size` past the two control bytes to the payload window that later becomes `original` and `input`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 3 bytes `02 14 10` (sha256 `d7981055d3a983019c9834250cacb91b9dbfc9c167beb1ccdbc0dbbc4410033f`). At this source step, byte 0 becomes `flags = 0x02`, byte 1 stays in the repetition-control slot, and `data += 2; size -= 2` leaves the single remaining payload byte `0x10` as the exact buffer later wrapped in `original` and copied into `input`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Project call site that reaches the saved MSan crash. `RegexMatcher::Match()` immediately queries `test.size()`, and the top MSan frame is libc++ `std::__1::basic_string::size()` reached from this statement.
sink.note: The saved stack is `std::__1::basic_string::size() -> RegexMatcher::Match:83 -> ScalarReferenceResult::Check:200 -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:268`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. This line rebuilds a second `std::string` from the stack-backed `original.c_str()` view, and the saved MSan store stack identifies it as the first project statement that copies uninitialized bytes into the path-visible `input` object.
root_cause.note: The staged metadata patch is unrelated to this file, so there is no patch-backed fix hunk for this obligation. The saved MSan evidence instead directly grounds line 246 as the first propagation from stack `original` into the later regex-matching path.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer attributes the poison to stack allocation of `original` in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`; on the exact witness path this is the stack `std::string` that wraps the remaining payload byte before line 246 copies from `original.c_str()`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved origin frame is symbolized at function line 234 in the instrumented build, while the exact staged declaration corresponding to stack object `original` is line 245.

parser_admitted.description: The exact remaining payload has `input.size() == 1`, so this early-return gate does not fire and execution continues into `ScalarReferenceResult::Check()`.
parser_admitted.condition: For witness `02 14 10`, bypassing the first two control bytes leaves exactly one payload byte, so neither the `< kMinInputLength` nor the `> kMaxInputLength` branch is taken.

evidence_limitations: The staged `patch.diff` / metadata `fixed_commit` do not touch `tests/fuzzer/flatbuffers_scalar_fuzzer.cc`, so `patch_resolves` is false and the trace is grounded by the saved vulnerable run rather than by a matching fix hunk.

The project-side chain is source-grounded only up to the statements MSan names. The exact libc++ internal field or SSO byte copied by `std::string(original.c_str())` and later consumed by `std::string::size()` is a standard-library implementation detail not exposed in FlatBuffers source, so the trace records only the witnessed project statements that trigger and consume that poisoned state.

fine_trace.note: Source step. From the exact 3-byte witness `02 14 10`, this code reads `flags = 0x02` from byte 0 and advances `data,size` past the two control bytes, so the remaining window is the single payload byte `0x10` that later becomes `original` and `input`.

The remaining payload from step 1 is wrapped in stack `std::string original` to guarantee NUL termination. The saved MSan origin says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `original` in this stack frame; the symbolized line in the trace is function line 234, while the exact staged declaration is line 245.

Root cause. The code immediately rebuilds a second string from `original.c_str()`. The saved MSan store stack identifies this line as the first point where uninitialized bytes were stored to memory on the crashing path, propagating state from stack `original` into `input`.
With `flags & flags_scalar_type == 0x2` from step 1, `Check()` selects the `int8` case and passes poisoned `input` into `IntegerRegex().Match()`.

`StripString` trims only tab, carriage return, newline, and space. For the exact payload byte `0x10`, both `find_first_not_of` and `find_last_not_of` resolve to index 0, so this call materializes `test` as a 1-byte substring of `input`. The saved MSan store stack names this caller line as the next propagation site into memory.

Sink. `RegexMatcher::Match()` immediately queries `test.size()`, and Stage 01's saved MSan report records the observed `use-of-uninitialized-value` here: frame 0 is libc++ `std::__1::basic_string::size()`, and this line is the first project frame on that stack.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSan origin reports `Uninitialized value was created by an allocation of 'original' in the stack frame of function 'LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput'` at line 234; the exact staged declaration corresponding to that stack object is line 245.

format.name: 3-byte flatbuffers scalar_fuzzer input
format.contract: The saved evidence proves only the exact staged 3-byte witness `02 14 10` (sha256 `d7981055d3a983019c9834250cacb91b9dbfc9c167beb1ccdbc0dbbc4410033f`). Byte 0 makes `flags & 0x0f == 0x2`, so `ScalarReferenceResult::Check` selects the `int8` / `IntegerRegex` arm. Byte 1 occupies the fuzzer's repetition-control slot; the crash happens before that later repetition loop matters. After the two control bytes are bypassed, the remaining single payload byte `0x10` is wrapped in stack `original`, copied into `input` via `std::string(original.c_str())`, and then sent through `RegexMatcher::Match`, where `test.size()` triggers the saved MSan use-of-uninitialized-value. The staged artifacts do not prove a broader trigger class or a patch-backed fix beyond this exact witness.
